title: BusinessFunction
description: A business behavior element that groups ongoing internal behavior by the competency, skill, knowledge or resource it requires (e.g. Accounting, Claims Handling, Procurement), performed by a BusinessRole or BusinessActor, with no defined start, end or ordered sequence of steps. Use BusinessProcess instead when the behavior is an ordered sequence of steps with a trigger and a defined end result (e.g. 'Handle Insurance Claim from submission to payout') rather than a standing area of competence. Use BusinessService instead when the element describes externally visible behavior from the consumer's perspective (what is offered), rather than the internal grouping of work that realizes it. Use BusinessInteraction instead when the behavior can only be performed jointly by two or more roles in a BusinessCollaboration rather than by a single role or actor. Use BusinessRole instead when the element names who holds responsibility (e.g. 'Claims Handler', 'Finance Department') rather than the behavior they perform (e.g. 'Claims Handling', 'Financial Accounting').

documentation.description: Free-text description of the competency area this function covers, its scope boundaries and the roles that perform it; set whenever the name alone does not make the grouped behavior unambiguous.

x-dr-evidence: top-level packages, modules or bounded contexts named after organizational competency areas (e.g. billing/, hr/, accounting/, procurement/) that own many related workflows rather than a single one

CODEOWNERS, team-ownership or service-catalog entries mapping a department or functional team to a group of modules, or permission scopes/menu sections grouped by functional area (e.g. 'finance:*', a 'Human Resources' navigation section)

architecture docs, capability or function maps, or ADRs listing functional areas of the business (e.g. a 'Business Functions' table or level-1 functional decomposition) referenced by code comments or module READMEs
